1.text_clean:
1. A rocket travels a distance of 3 km in 10 s.
What is the order of magnitude of $\frac{\text{the speed of the rocket}}{\text{the speed of light in a vacuum}}$?
A. $-5$
B. $-6$
C. $-7$
D. $-8$

2.text_clean:
2. The variation with time of the displacement of an object is shown.
[Graph: displacement / m (0 to 12) against time / s (0 to 10); straight line from (0, 0) to (8, 10), then straight line down to (10, 8)]
What are the average speed and average velocity of the object over the 10 s time interval?
Average speed / m s$^{-1}$ | Average velocity / m s$^{-1}$
A. 0.8 | 0.8
B. 0.8 | 1.2
C. 1.2 | 0.8
D. 1.2 | 1.2

3.text_clean:
3. A mass is suspended by a light string from the roof of a car. The car is accelerating up an incline.
[Diagram: car on an incline rising to the left, arrow showing acceleration up the slope; mass hangs on a string tilted back from the vertical]
What is the free-body diagram for the mass?
[Options A–D: free-body diagrams of the mass. A: tension along string (up-left), weight down, and a horizontal force to the right. B: tension along string (up-left) and weight down only. C: shorter tension along string and longer weight down. D: tension along string, weight down, and a force to the right angled slightly downwards]

4.text_clean:
4. An object is travelling with velocity 5 m s$^{-1}$. The object then accelerates to 15 m s$^{-1}$ in the same direction.
What is the variation with time of the acceleration of the object?
[Four graphs of acceleration / m s$^{-2}$ (0 to 12) against time / s (0 to 6).
A: acceleration increases linearly from 0 at t = 0 to 10 at t = 5 s, then drops to 0.
B: acceleration 0 until t = 1 s, jumps to 10, then decreases linearly to 0 at t = 6 s.
C: acceleration 10 between t = 2 s and t = 4 s, zero otherwise.
D: acceleration 5 between t = 2 s and t = 4 s, zero otherwise.]

5.text_clean:
5. The angle $\theta$ between a ramp and a horizontal surface slowly increases from zero. An object on the ramp does not slide as $\theta$ increases.
[Diagram: object resting on a ramp inclined at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal]
The frictional force on the object is
A. constant.
B. negligible.
C. proportional to $\cos\theta$.
D. proportional to $\sin\theta$.

6.text_clean:
6. A spring of negligible mass is compressed and placed between two stationary masses $m$ and $M$. The mass of $M$ is twice that of $m$. The spring is released so that the masses move in opposite directions.
[Diagram: compressed spring between block m and block M]
What is $\frac{\text{kinetic energy of } m}{\text{kinetic energy of } M}$?
A. $\frac{1}{2}$
B. 1
C. 2
D. 4

7.text_clean:
7. An object of mass $M$ is accelerated vertically upwards by a motor at a constant acceleration. The object is initially at rest and reaches a vertical speed of 4.0 m s$^{-1}$ in 2.0 s.
[Diagram: motor winding a cable lifting mass M vertically upwards from the floor; arrow labelled direction of motion]
What is the average power output of the motor?
A. $8M$
B. $24M$
C. $32M$
D. $48M$

8.text_clean:
8. An object is released from rest at X and slides to Y. The vertical distance between X and Y is 10 m. During the motion, 20 % of the object's initial gravitational potential energy is lost as friction.
[Diagram: curved slope from X at the top down to Y, vertical height 10 m]
What is the speed of the object at Y?
A. $\frac{16}{\sqrt{g}}$
B. $2\sqrt{g}$
C. $4\sqrt{g}$
D. $8g$

9.text_clean:
9. A fixed mass of an ideal gas expands slowly at constant temperature in a container.
Three statements about the gas molecules during the expansion are:
I. They collide with the walls of the container at a reduced rate.
II. They travel further on average between each collision.
III. Their average kinetic energy decreases as the gas expands.
Which statements are correct?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

10.text_clean:
10. A balloon of volume $V$ contains 10 mg of an ideal gas at a pressure $P$. An additional mass of the gas is added without changing the temperature of the balloon. This change causes the volume to increase to $2V$ and the pressure to increase to $3P$.
What is the mass of gas **added** to the balloon?
A. 5 mg
B. 15 mg
C. 50 mg
D. 60 mg

11.text_clean:
11. A pipe containing air is closed at one end and open at the other. The third harmonic standing wave for this pipe has a frequency of 150 Hz.
What other frequency is possible for a standing wave in this pipe?
A. 25 Hz
B. 50 Hz
C. 75 Hz
D. 300 Hz

12.text_clean:
12. A longitudinal wave is travelling through a medium. The variation with distance $d$ of the displacement $x$ of the particles in the medium at time $t$ is shown.
Which point is at the centre of a compression?
[Graph: displacement $x$ (positive = displacement of particles to the right, negative = to the left) against distance $d$, a sinusoid starting at a positive maximum. Point A: where $x$ crosses zero going from positive to negative; point B: at the negative minimum (trough); point C: where $x$ crosses zero going from negative to positive; point D: at the positive maximum (crest)]

13.text_clean:
13. Unpolarized light of intensity $I$ and amplitude $A$ passes through a polarizing filter.
[Diagram: incident light of intensity $I$ passing through a polarizing filter; transmitted light emerges]
What is the amplitude of the light transmitted by the polarizing filter?
A. $\frac{A^2}{2}$
B. $\frac{A}{4}$
C. $\frac{A}{2}$
D. $\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

14.text_clean:
14. An electromagnetic wave enters a medium of lower refractive index.
Three statements are made:
I. The wavelength of the wave has increased.
II. The frequency of the wave has decreased.
III. The speed of the wave has increased.
What is true about the properties of the wave?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

15.text_clean:
15. Three point charges, +Q, +Q and −Q, are fixed at the three corners of a square.
What is the direction of the electric field at the fourth corner?
[Diagram: square with −Q at top right, +Q at bottom left and +Q at bottom right; the empty fourth corner is top left, with four arrows drawn from it: A points right and slightly up, B points up and slightly right, C points up and to the left, D points down and to the left]

16.text_clean:
16. Two resistors of equal resistance $R$ are connected with two cells of emf $\varepsilon$ and $2\varepsilon$. Both cells have negligible internal resistance.
[Circuit: cell $\varepsilon$ on the left in series with resistor X along the top wire to a junction; second resistor connected vertically between the junction and the bottom wire; cell $2\varepsilon$ on the right connected across the second resistor]
What is the current in the resistor labelled X?
A. $\frac{\varepsilon}{2R}$
B. $\frac{3\varepsilon}{2R}$
C. $\frac{\varepsilon}{R}$
D. $\frac{3\varepsilon}{R}$

17.text_clean:
17. Two secondary cells require recharging. Which circuit will recharge both cells?
[Four circuit diagrams A–D, each with a recharger (− terminal left, + terminal right) connected across two cells in parallel; the diagrams differ in the orientation of each cell's positive and negative terminals]

18.text_clean:
18. A negatively charged sphere is falling through a magnetic field.
[Diagram: north pole of magnet on the left, south pole of magnet on the right; negatively charged sphere moving vertically downwards between the poles]
What is the direction of the magnetic force acting on the sphere?
A. To the left of the page
B. To the right of the page
C. Out of the page
D. Into the page

19.text_clean:
19. A mass on the end of a string is rotating on a frictionless table in circular motion of radius $R_1$ and undergoes an angular displacement of $\theta$ in time $t$.
[Diagram: mass moving in a horizontal circle of radius $R_1$ on a table]
The string tension is kept constant, but the angular displacement of the mass is increased to $2\theta$ in time $t$. The radius of the motion changes to $R_2$.
What is $R_2$?
A. $\frac{R_1}{4}$
B. $2R_1$
C. $4R_1$
D. $R_1 \times R_1$

20.text_clean:
20. The gravitational field strength at the surface of the Earth is often taken to be 9.8 N kg$^{-1}$.
The use of this value to calculate the weight of an object **above** the surface of the Earth is
A. a paradigm shift in our understanding of gravity.
B. an attempt to model gravitational fields.
C. an outcome from a peer review.
D. an approximation used for estimation purposes.

21.text_clean:
21. White light is incident on gas at very low pressure. The light passing through the gas is analysed.
What phenomenon is being investigated?
A. Absorption spectrum
B. Emission spectrum
C. Photoelectric effect
D. Polarization

22.text_clean:
22. A student measures the count rate of a radioactive sample with time in a laboratory. The background count in the laboratory is 30 counts per second.
Count rate / counts per second | Time / s
150 | 0
90 | 20
What is the time at which the student measures a count rate of 45 counts per second?
A. 30 s
B. 40 s
C. 60 s
D. 80 s

23.text_clean:
23. Three statements about the binding energy are provided.
I. The binding energy is the energy required to completely separate the nucleons.
II. The binding energy is equivalent, in units of energy, to the mass defect when a nucleus is formed from its nucleons.
III. The binding energy is the energy released when a nucleus is formed from its nucleons.
Which statements are true?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

24.text_clean:
24. The following reaction is proposed for the collision of a proton p and a neutron n.
$p + n \rightarrow p + \pi^0$
The neutral pion $\pi^0$ consists of an up quark and an anti-up quark.
Which conservation law does this equation violate?
A. Baryon number
B. Charge
C. Lepton number
D. Strangeness

25.text_clean:
25. Wind generator X has a maximum power output $P_X$ for a particular wind speed. For the same wind speed, wind generator Y has a maximum power output $P_Y$.
The blade radius of Y is three times the blade radius of X. Y is twice as efficient as X.
What is $\frac{P_Y}{P_X}$?
A. $\frac{3}{2}$
B. $\frac{9}{2}$
C. 6
D. 18

26.text_clean:
26. What is **not** correct about a photovoltaic cell?
A. It has an output power that is related to the surface area of the cell.
B. It generates an alternating current.
C. It absorbs energy over a range of photon frequencies.
D. It can be used to store energy in a secondary cell.

27.text_clean:
27. A planet has an albedo of 0.30. A simplified energy balance for the planet is shown.
[Diagram: incoming intensity 100 W m$^{-2}$ arrives at the planet surface; reflected intensity arrow leaves; arrow of 60 W m$^{-2}$ from the atmosphere back down to the surface; arrow radiated up from the surface through the atmosphere]
What is the intensity radiated by the surface of the planet?
A. 70 W m$^{-2}$
B. 90 W m$^{-2}$
C. 100 W m$^{-2}$
D. 130 W m$^{-2}$

28.text_clean:
28. A mass oscillating in simple harmonic motion on the end of a spring has an amplitude $x_0$ and a total energy $E_T$. The mass on the spring is doubled and made to oscillate with the same amplitude $x_0$.
What is the total energy of the oscillating system after the change?
A. $E_T$
B. $\sqrt{2}E_T$
C. $2E_T$
D. $4E_T$

29.text_clean:
29. Monochromatic light is incident on a single slit to form a diffraction pattern on a screen. The width of the single slit is then halved.
What are the change in the width of the central maximum and the change in the maximum intensity of the pattern?
Change in width of central maximum | Change in maximum intensity of pattern
A. decrease | increase
B. decrease | decrease
C. increase | decrease
D. increase | increase

30.text_clean:
30. Two spheres have the same positive charge. A point M is midway between the two spheres.
[Diagram: two positively charged spheres joined by a line, M at the midpoint]
Along the line joining the spheres, what is true about the electrical field and the electric potential at M?
Electric field | Electric potential
A. zero | minimum positive value
B. maximum | minimum positive value
C. zero | maximum positive value
D. maximum | maximum positive value

31.text_clean:
31. The mass of Mars is about ten times that of the Moon. The radius of Mars is about twice that of the Moon.
What is the $\frac{\text{escape speed from Mars}}{\text{escape speed from Moon}}$?
A. $\sqrt{5}$
B. $2\sqrt{5}$
C. 5
D. 25

32.text_clean:
32. A single loop of wire of resistance 10 Ω has its plane perpendicular to a changing magnetic field.
The graph shows the variation with time of the magnetic flux linked through the loop of wire.
[Graph: magnetic flux / Wb against time / s; flux rises linearly from 0 at t = 0 to 40 Wb at t = 2 s, stays at 40 Wb until t = 5 s, then falls linearly to 0 at t = 9 s]
What is the maximum current in the loop of wire?
A. 1.0 A
B. 2.0 A
C. 4.0 A
D. 20 A

33.text_clean:
33. An ac generator produces a root mean square (rms) voltage $V$. What is the peak output voltage when the frequency is doubled?
A. $\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}V$
B. $\frac{V}{2\sqrt{2}}$
C. $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}V$
D. $2\sqrt{2}V$

34.text_clean:
34. Step-up transformers are used in the distribution of electrical energy to
A. reduce the danger of electrical shock to humans.
B. decrease the potential difference between the ends of long-distance transmission lines.
C. allow direct current appliances to work in domestic applications.
D. decrease the electrical current in long-distance transmission lines.

35.text_clean:
35. Two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in series to a cell as shown. The capacitance of $C_1$ is four times the capacitance of $C_2$. The charge stored on $C_1$ is $q_1$ and the charge stored on $C_2$ is $q_2$.
[Circuit: cell in series with capacitors $C_2$ and $C_1$]
What is $\frac{q_1}{q_2}$?
A. $\frac{1}{4}$
B. $\frac{4}{5}$
C. 1
D. 4

36.text_clean:
36. A charged 200 μF capacitor is placed in series with a 10 kΩ resistor. At time $t = 0$, the current is $I$.
[Circuit: 200 μF capacitor connected in a loop with a 10 kΩ resistor]
What is the time taken for the current in the resistor to be $\frac{I}{e^3}$?
A. 2 s
B. 3 s
C. 6 s
D. 8 s

37.text_clean:
37. Light of frequency $f$ is incident on a metallic surface of work function $W$. Photoelectrons with a maximum kinetic energy $E_{max}$ are emitted. The frequency of the incident light is changed to $2f$.
What is true about the maximum kinetic energy and the work function?
Maximum kinetic energy | Work function
A. less than $2E_{max}$ | unchanged
B. less than $2E_{max}$ | greater than $W$
C. greater than $2E_{max}$ | unchanged
D. greater than $2E_{max}$ | greater than $W$

38.text_clean:
38. What is the variation of nuclear density $\rho$ with nucleon number $A$?
[Four sketch graphs of $\rho$ against $A$: A: straight line increasing from a positive intercept; B: horizontal line (constant); C: rises steeply to a maximum then decreases; D: increases and levels off towards a constant asymptote]

39.text_clean:
39. The uncertainty in the energy required for pair production is 3 MeV. What is the uncertainty in the lifetime of the pair?
A. $10^{-7}$ s
B. $10^{-12}$ s
C. $10^{-17}$ s
D. $10^{-22}$ s

40.text_clean:

[Diagram (not to scale): energy levels n = 1, n = 2, n = 3; transition X from n = 2 to n = 1; transition Y from n = 3 to n = 1]
What is the $\frac{\text{wavelength emitted in transition X}}{\text{wavelength emitted in transition Y}}$?
A. $\frac{1}{2}$
B. $\frac{27}{32}$
